Asha — thanks, received.

I've attached a first-pass "egress catalog" which is intended to be the single source of truth for the firewall team. Key points up front:
- We operate two distinct egress classes for Private deployments: control-plane (low-bandwidth telemetry/auth) and data-plane (model pulls, downloads).
- Control-plane uses a small set of stable IP ranges; data-plane may use region-prefixed ranges and a limited set of CDN endpoints for model artifact distribution.
- We can support either direct IP allowlisting or FQDN-based allowlisting via your proxy; however, FQDN allowlisting requires SNI passthrough (TLS) and may necessitate outbound DNS whitelisting for the model-registry domains.

High-level outbound requirements (summary):
- Control plane (required):
  - IP ranges: 34.214.120.0/22, 52.12.64.0/22, 18.197.32.0/23
  - Ports: 443 (HTTPS), 123 (NTP) — NTP only if you opt into detailed telemetry timestamps
  - Protocols/SNI: TLS1.2+/SNI required; client cert optional for MTLS customers
- Model artifact downloads (recommended pinning):
  - FQDNs: models.redwood.ai, artifacts-cdn.redwood.ai, s3-us-east-1.amazonaws.com (use region-specific endpoints where applicable)
  - Ports: 443 only
- Telemetry/billing endpoints: telemetry.redwood.ai (443), billing-api.redwood.ai (443)
- Fallbacks: if the primary regional CIDRs are unreachable, we can failover to a global CDN set: 52.58.128.0/20 (global-cdn-redwood) — enable only if you accept broader egress during incidents

Operational notes:
- IP rotation: control-plane ranges are semistable — we publish any changes 30 days in advance and provide a signed attestation when ranges change.
- Evidence pack: we'll include a short matrix (IP -> purpose) and a diffs file to simplify PRs on your firewall config repo.

I've attached: redwood-egress-catalog-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet with CIDRs, ports, service owners) and a diff-style text file showing the proposed firewall ruleset. Please confirm whether you prefer that we deliver the artifact URLs as IPs or FQDNs for your environment.

Next step: can your infra/security owner confirm they can open the listed IP ranges and permit SNI passthrough for the FQDN set? If you prefer a proxy-based pattern, we can provide example ALB/NGINX configs.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: FW: Outbound controls for Redwood private endpoint (operational constraints)

Ben/Jordan — quick operational notes from infra that we should surface to Neptune before they ship rules:

1) Data-plane model pulls: by default our model distribution uses region-localized edge caches. If Neptune wants strict per-IP allowlisting, they must allow the full region block (we've listed examples below). Otherwise recommend allowing the FQDNs (artifacts-cdn.redwood.ai) and enabling SNI passthrough on their TLS proxy so we don't break certificate name validation.

2) Control-plane NAT binding: we run NAT-gateway pairs per-region. The current region CIDRs that will matter to Neptune (us-east-1) are the three control-plane CIDRs Jordan listed. For additional safety we can offer a static egress proxy (customer-facing) that pins outbound to a single IP per-region (extra cost / reserved).

3) DNS & proxy interplay: if Neptune uses an outbound proxy that inspects TLS, we need either (a) MTLS with certs we trust, or (b) SOCKS/TCP pass-through for SNI. We cannot guarantee service delivery if the proxy terminates TLS and replaces certs without MTLS.

4) Ports & monitoring: telemetry requires 443 only. If they accept us sending aggregated NTP telemetry, enable outbound 123 to our control-plane NTP IP (18.197.32.12). Otherwise we'll jitter timestamps but still operate.

Action items for Neptune: please confirm the following by EOD Wednesday, Sep 9:
- Accept the control-plane CIDRs listed or request static proxy IPs
- Confirm whether their proxy performs TLS termination (and if so, whether MTLS is possible)
- Provide the name of the firewall config repo and preferred PR cadence (we'll prepare a diff)

Thanks — circling in Laura for compliance signoff on the attestation language.

-Marissa
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Jordan/Marissa — thanks for the detailed breakdown and the spreadsheet. We reviewed internally with our network team and have a couple of redlines and a confirmation:

Redlines:
- We require that model artifact downloads be pinned to FQDNs and SNI passthrough (we will not open broad CDN IP ranges by default). Please confirm Redwood will support TLS SNI passthrough without interception.
- We ask that you provide an attestation PDF for control-plane CIDR stability for the next 90 days; any changes during that period must be notified 30 days in advance.

We can accept the control-plane CIDRs as listed provided you supply the attestation. For fallback behavior, Neptune requests that you document the exact global fallback ranges and mark them as "incident-only" (we will not allow those in our regular policy).

Next steps:
- Please upload the attestation to the linked HubSpot deal and share a CR/PR to our firewall repo: https://git.neptune.internal/firewall-configs/pulls (we will review and apply).
- Rajiv (cc) will follow up about potential edge caching overlap with Akamai — he may request additional FQDNs or CDN hostnames.

Acceptance: Neptune agrees to permit the following control-plane CIDRs in production after we receive the attestation: 34.214.120.0/22, 52.12.64.0/22, 18.197.32.0/23.

Thank you — looking forward to the attestation and the small PR.
